proton.def: A positively charged particle in the nucleus of an atom; the number of protons decides which element an atom is.

neutron.def: A particle with no charge in the nucleus of an atom, with almost the same mass as a proton.

electron.def: A tiny negatively charged particle outside the nucleus; it has about 1/1800 of the mass of a proton.

nucleus.def: The small, dense center of an atom, made of protons and neutrons, which holds almost all of the atom's mass.

atomic-number.def: The number of protons in an atom's nucleus, which identifies the element (carbon is 6, oxygen 8).

mass-number.def: The number of protons plus neutrons in an atom's nucleus, written as in carbon-14 or ¹⁴C.

isotope.def: Atoms of the same element (same number of protons) with different numbers of neutrons, and so different masses.

ion.def: An atom or group of atoms with an electric charge, because it has gained or lost electrons.

cation.def: A positive ion: it has fewer electrons than protons, such as Na⁺.

anion.def: A negative ion: it has more electrons than protons, such as Cl⁻.

relative-abundance.def: The share of an element's atoms that are one particular isotope, usually given as a percent.

mass-spectrum.def: A graph from a mass spectrometer showing the masses of the ions in a sample and how many of each there are; for an element, one peak per isotope.

mass-to-charge.def: The mass of an ion divided by its charge (m/z), the quantity a mass spectrometer sorts by; for a 1+ ion it equals the mass.

average-atomic-mass.def: The mean mass of an element's atoms, weighting each isotope's mass by its relative abundance; the value on the periodic table.
